sam: hey all — first day! trying to bootstrap my workstation (Intel MacBook). want a single setup that works for python/node/go/rust. hitting issues with asdf python & openssl during build. any recommended quick checklist?

maya: welcome!! :tada: for intel macs brew+asdf is pretty solid. quick checklist i send new hires: brew, asdf, git, 1password, docker, rustup (for rust), and set up ssh/gpg.

kevin: if you're seeing openssl errors for python builds, usually need to point to brew's openssl. on intel brew lives in /usr/local. set these env vars before building python: 
```bash
export LDFLAGS="-L/usr/local/opt/openssl@1.1/lib"
export CPPFLAGS="-I/usr/local/opt/openssl@1.1/include"
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="/usr/local/opt/openssl@1.1/lib/pkgconfig"
```
then `asdf install python 3.11.5` should work.

sam: thanks, trying that now. do we pin versions via .tool-versions in dotfiles?

devex: yes — we check in a project-level .tool-versions per repo. for your global dev machine i keep a `~/.tool-versions-local` that's symlinked in my dotfiles and not checked in. also run `asdf plugin-add python` / `nodejs` / `golang` / `rust` first. for nodejs you'll need `gpg` to verify distros — install gpg via brew.

maya: if you use asdf + node, remember the nodejs plugin needs the nodejs-release-team gpg keys: https://github.com/asdf-vm/asdf-nodejs#installation

sam: any dotfiles tips? i'm on zsh.

kevin: dotfiles: we have an examples repo in the handbook but typical pattern: 
- ~/.config/redwood/dotfiles (private for anything with secrets)
- symlink ~/.zshrc -> dotfiles/zsh/.zshrc 
- put 1password CLI helper init in .zshrc so `op` is available early

sam: ssh/gpg: i want to sign commits and enable agent forwarding to a remote build vm. what do you all use?

maya: we use gpg for commit signing and 1password SSH agent for keys on laptop. steps: generate ed25519 key for ssh, put pub in GitHub, add gpg key and configure git user.signingkey. then enable agent and forwarding: 
```bash
# start agent
eval "$(ssh-agent -s)"
ssh-add --apple-use-keychain ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
# ~/.ssh/config snippet
Host *
  AddKeysToAgent yes
  UseKeychain yes
  ForwardAgent yes
```

sam: nice. where do i find the REDWOOD_API_KEY or credentials I need for local dev?

devex: secrets (API keys, infra creds) are in 1Password vault named "Redwood - Developer Secrets". reach out to @devex if you don't have access and we'll add you. typical env vars for local: 
- REDWOOD_API_KEY (for talking to staging endpoints)
- REDWOOD_ENV=development
- REDWOOD_REGION (us-east-1 by default)
we recommend putting these in an envrc or direnv file per project rather than in your global shell.

onboarding-bot: reminder: new hire checklist step 4 incomplete — join #devex and confirm 1Password access.

sam: thanks all, asdf python build succeeded after LDFLAGS/CPPFLAGS. next up: node + yarn. i'll ping if I hit more snags. :raised_hands:

kevin: for node, `asdf install nodejs 18.16.0` + `npm i -g corepack` then `corepack enable` to get yarn/pnpm wrappers. works well.

maya: ping us in #new-hires or #devex if anything else. also feel free to ask for a quick screenshare.

sam: will do — appreciate the help!"
